Subject: Private cutover — intermittent post-cutover packet loss (captured)

Hi Mateo,

We completed the private VPC cutover to Redwood Private earlier today (cutover window 15:00-16:00 PST). Since the change we've seen intermittent packet loss and a number of failed API calls from our on-prem services to the private endpoint. Symptoms: ~0.5-2% packet loss spikes every 10-30 minutes, observed across multiple hosts. The attached tcpdump shows repeated retransmits and occasional ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages.

We've also pulled a quick traceroute and included it in the pcap bundle. Can you help triage routing / MTU / SG issues on your side? Our NOC is standing by and we've opened a ticket with CloudCarrier (our carrier) — their NOC (noc@cloudcarrier.net) has been included.

Attachments: skyview-trace-20261208.pcap, traceroute.txt

Thanks,

Thanks for the packet capture, Samuel — I’ve ingested it and started an initial triage. High level: I see a mix of retransmits and periodic ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages which points to an MTU mismatch somewhere in the path; there are also bursts that line up with SNAT port churn on our edge (possible ephemeral port exhaustion causing short failures).

Immediate asks:
- Can you paste the output of: ip route get <private-endpoint-ip> from one host and the traceroute you ran?
- Can you confirm your on‑prem edge MTU (we need the NIC MTU and any VPN/encapsulation overhead)
- If possible, collect conntrack counters and ephemeral port usage around the spike (ss -s; /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range)

Internal: looping in Vanessa, Marissa and Karthik to coordinate. Vanessa — can you check the private route table and SNAT pool usage for the tenant? Marissa — can you surface any recent SG changes around the private endpoint and pull flow logs for the time window? Karthik — if we need an MSS clamp on the VPN or VPN GW MTU tweak, can you validate options and timing?

I’ll keep this thread as the single source of truth. We may need a quick war-room if the carrier sees any mid-path fragmentation.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez

Thanks, team. Quick update from our side — results of the checks you asked for below. I’m including the tcpdump excerpt and traceroute output inline.

- ip route get <10.21.5.14> from host-a:
  10.21.5.14 via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0 src 10.0.1.22 uid 1000

- Host NIC MTU: 1500
- VPN peer MTU (on-prem SRX): 1476 (this includes 24 bytes for IPsec esp overhead)
- Conntrack: high-water mark around 18k entries (ss -s shows ephemeral ports in normal range)

Traceroute (excerpt):
 1 10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1) 1.2 ms
 2 198.51.100.10 (198.51.100.10) 3.9 ms
 3 203.0.113.17 (203.0.113.17) 7.1 ms
 4 * * *
 5 203.0.113.21 (203.0.113.21) 12.5 ms (ICMP frag needed seen here)

The pcap shows TCP retransmits immediately after the host-to-endpoint flows exceed ~1428 bytes (payload) and we see "fragmentation needed" ICMP from 203.0.113.21 back to the host.

CloudCarrier NOC (on this thread) says there is a DCI XOR overlay in the carrier path that adds ~38 bytes during the window. They suspect the SRX peer MTU + carrier overlay pushes the effective path MTU below the host MTU and we are hitting the break.

If we need a temporary fix, we can either reduce host MTU to 1400 (we prefer not to do that fleet-wide unless required), or enable MSS clamping on the SRX VPN or at Redwood’s VPN egress.

Samuel

From: mateo_alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Liu <samuel.liu@skyviewhealth.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, NOC (CloudCarrier) <noc@cloudcarrier.net>
Date: 2026-12-10T09:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private cutover — intermittent post-cutover packet loss (captured)

Team — summary and remediation plan based on the captures and carrier confirmation:

Findings:
- Effective path MTU across the private link is ~1428 bytes due to SRX IPsec overhead (24B) + carrier overlay (38B) combined with host MTU 1500 — this triggers ICMP "fragmentation needed" and results in retransmits for large payloads.
- No evidence of sustained SNAT port exhaustion or SG deny rules firing in flow logs — ephemeral port ranges are healthy.

Action plan (agreed):
1) Immediate (temporary, low-risk) — apply MSS clamping on the Redwood VPN egress for the tenant to 1400 bytes. This will avoid fragmentation without changing customer host MTU. Target ETA: 2026-12-10 11:00 PST. (Karthik to execute and validate).
2) Mid-term — coordinate with SkyView NOC and CloudCarrier to align MTU settings on the SRX and carrier DCI; goal: eliminate double-counting of overhead and lift path MTU toward 1460+.
3) Validation — run a 4-hour traffic test post-change and collect pcap/traceroute; if no retransmits/ICMP frag, we will close the incident.
4) Documentation — update runbook-private-cutover.pdf with MTU checklist and a note to validate carrier overlays prior to cutover.

Marissa: since flow logs look clean, please add a short note to the runbook about SG audit steps we used. Samuel: please confirm by noon PST whether applying MSS clamp on our end is acceptable for you as a temporary mitigation.

I’ll open NETOPS-1227 and post the postmortem there after validation.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
